description: MESSENGER successfully flew by Mercury on October 6, 2008, using Mercury’s gravity to perturb the probe’s path and to help put it on track to become, in March 2011, the first spacecraft ever to orbit the innermost planet in the Solar System. This image, acquired about 89 minutes before the craft’s closest approach to Mercury, resembles the optical navigation images taken leading up to the flyby. This Wide Angle Camera image is one of 11 viewed through different narrow-band color filters, the set of which enable detailed color studies of this area. In addition, the Narrow Angle Camera (NAC) acquired a high-resolution mosaic of most of this thin crescent view of Mercury at a resolution better than 0.5 kilometers/pixel (0.3 miles/pixel) that enabled the MESSENGER team to explore this newly imaged region of Mercury’s surface in more detail. NASA Media Usage Guidelines Credit: NASA/Johns Hopkins University Applied Physics Laboratory/Carnegie Institution of Washington Image Number: PIA11247 Date: October 6, 2008

title: MESSENGER Encounters Mercury

description: Space shuttle Discovery's vertical stabilizer and orbital maneuvering system (OMS) pods are backdropped by the blackness of space and a colorful sunrise on Earth below. This view was taken through the orbiter's aft flight deck viewing windows during the STS-26 mission in 1988. STS-26 was NASA's first crewed spaceflight mission after the Challenger disaster on January 28, 1986. NASA Media Usage Guidelines Credit: NASA Image Number: s26-46-048 Date: October 3, 1988
label: Original
title: Sunrise as Seen from Space Shuttle Discovery
